findings.issue: The skill README adds --extend=N and --extend-minutes=M but leaves out two operator-facing limits. First, the extension keeps the run's stop policy, so under the default policy an extended run can re-stop at its first convergence check. Second, --extend refuses fan-out. The root README (line 255) and references/protocol/loop-protocol.md (Completed-run extension, Convergence window) state both, so the skill README is the one surface describing the flag without them. Add a sentence saying the extension is single-executor only, and that a run meant to be extended should be created with --convergence-mode=off or --stop-policy=max-iterations.

evidence.cmd: grep -c -i 're-stop\|refuses fan-out' .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-review/README.md; grep -n -o 'It keeps the stop policy the run was created with, so under the default policy it can re-stop at once' README.md

findings.issue: This file is outside the lane's assigned list, but the S6 lens names it. The newest root release notes at HEAD 83af96cb5af are v4.1.0.0, which is already tagged on origin, so the release is published and closed. The entry does not describe this scope's user-visible deep-review additions: --depth-mode=expansive, --extend=N for review, custom review dimensions and the review minIterations floor. The root README section at line 255 does describe them. No open root release entry carries them, so they reach no release notes until the operator opens a new skilled entry.
